title: Adjectives (Prepositional Case)
description: Adjective endings in the prepositional case
intro: The prepositional case is used after в/на (location), о/об (about), and при (in the presence of). Adjective endings in prepositional are straightforward: masculine and neuter take -ом/-ем, feminine takes -ой/-ей (same as genitive/dative/instrumental!), and plural takes -ых/-их. Notice that masculine/neuter prepositional (-ом) differs from dative (-ому) by just one letter!
rules: The prepositional case is triggered by в/на (location), о/об (about), and при — it NEVER appears without a preposition.
Masculine/neuter prepositional -ом looks very similar to dative -ому — the missing -у is the key difference.
Feminine prepositional (-ой/-ей) is identical to genitive, dative, and instrumental — context determines the case.
Plural prepositional (-ых/-их) is identical to genitive plural — again, prepositions and context clarify which case is meant.
examples: Я живу в большом городе. (I live in a big city.), masc
Мы говорим о русской литературе. (We are talking about Russian literature.), fem
Дети играют в новом парке. (The children play in the new park.), masc
Она думает о старых друзьях. (She thinks about old friends.), plural

В (in) requires prepositional for location. Дом is masculine. Masculine prepositional ending: -ом or -ому?
О (about) requires prepositional. Друзья is plural. Plural prepositional ending: -ых or -ыми?

explanations: О requires prepositional. Feminine: русская → русской (ending -ой).
В requires prepositional for location. Masculine: новый → новом (ending -ом).
О requires prepositional. Plural: старые → старых (ending -ых).
В requires prepositional. Masculine: большой → большом (ending -ом).
О requires prepositional. Feminine: интересная → интересной (ending -ой).
